Scheme: R76/2006 → scheme A? R76 scheme... For R76 (non-automatic weighing instruments), it's actually under the OIML Certificate Scheme — scheme A. The cert number format R76/2006-GB1-09.02. Scheme is typically "A" for these OIML CS certs. Hmm, the schema says scheme (A|B). R76 certs under MAA are scheme A. I'll use "A".

- type_designations: ["WPI-700"] — also WPI-701 (single scale) and WPI-702 (dual scale) are designated instruments using it. Those are the weighing instruments designated WPI-701 and WPI-702. Hmm, the certified pattern is the indicator WPI-700. The instruments WPI-701 and WPI-702 are mentioned as designs. I could include them in type_designations as they're mentioned type identifiers. The rule: "all type/model identifiers mentioned". So type_designations: ["WPI-700", "WPI-701", "WPI-702"].

Module designation: for R76, modules... The indicator is a module. Not explicitly stated. Maybe omit or "Not applicable"? Not stated in the doc; per rule 8 don't fabricate. I could set null. Schema allows null. I'll omit or set null. I'll omit.

Components: The cert names sub-assemblies:
- Teraoka TPB-2930 CPU
- Teraoka TPB-03324 6 wire A/D converter
- Touch screen (colour TFT-LCD module)
- Waterproof metallic enclosure

Alternative construction:
- A/D board drawing No TPB-03484-00-00 Rev 0 (A/D converter TPB-03484)

So components[] entries:
1. role: "CPU", type_designations: ["Teraoka TPB-2930"]
2. role: "A/D converter", type_designations: ["Teraoka TPB-03324", "Teraoka TPB-03484"], alternatives: "OR"? Actually the alternative construction uses TPB-03484 instead of TPB-03324. The two technical data tables differ. So we could model two configurations: original and alternative. Alternatively config_level with axis "construction" (original vs alternative).

Actually the cert covers two variants of the indicator: the original construction and the alternative construction (modified A/D board, main board and power supply). Attributes differ: power supply voltage (100-230 vs 100-240 VAC), load cell excitation voltage (10 Vdc vs 3.3 Vdc), min load cell impedance (87 Ω vs 43 Ω), max load cell impedance (440 Ω vs 1100 Ω), operating temperature (-10 to +30 °C vs -10 to +40 °C), load cell cable (750 m/mm² vs 1.5 m).

This is a good case for config_level with axis "construction_variant" with conditions "standard" and "alternative".

Characteristics type_level (common to both):
- max_number_of_scale_intervals: 6000 single interval; 3000 per partial weighing range multi-interval with max two weighing ranges. This is complex; could be recorded as value string or separate entries. Value 6000 for single interval. Hmm. Let me record:
  - maximum_number_of_scale_intervals: {value: 6000, footnote? no} plus a description. Maybe two characteristics: maximum_number_of_scale_intervals_single_interval: 6000; maximum_number_of_scale_intervals_per_partial_range: 3000. And max_number_of_weighing_ranges: 2.
- dual_interval_range: Max₁ ≤ 50% Max₂ — formula. Value string "Max1 ≤ 50% Max2" — canonical: "maximum capacity of first range ≤ 50% of second"? Keep as string value: "Max1 ≤ 0.5 × Max2"? Better keep as given: "Max1 <= 50% Max2". Rules say no LaTeX; subscript fine. I'll record as string "Max1 ≤ 50% Max2".
- maximum_tare: -50% of Max → value -50, unit "%"? The value is "-50% Max". Could record as {value: -50, unit_symbol: "%"} with a reference... Simpler: value: -50, unit_symbol: "%", maybe attribute "maximum_tare" and separate note. I'll do value -50, unit "%".
- maximum_preset_tare: "- Max1" → value string "Max1"? Hmm "- Max1". Value could be "−Max1" formula string. Record as {value: "-Max1"}? Keep string "-Max1".
- minimum_input_voltage_per_verification_scale_interval: 0.67 µV
- measuring_range_minimum_voltage: 0 mV
- measuring_range_maximum_voltage: 40 mV
- fraction_of_maximum_permittable_error (pind): 0.5
- load_cell_connection: 6-wire shielded (alternative construction states this; original says "Load cell 6-wire connection" under interfaces — so 6-wire for both)
- power_supply_frequency: {min: 50, max: 60} Hz

Config-level (construction axis):
- power_supply_voltage: standard 100-230 V (AC), alternative 100-240 V (AC)
- load_cell_excitation_voltage: standard 10 Vdc, alternative 3.3 Vdc
- minimum_load_cell_impedance: 87 Ω vs 43 Ω
- maximum_load_cell_impedance: 440 Ω vs 1100 Ω
- operating_temperature_range: -10 to +30 °C vs -10 to +40 °C
- load_cell_cable_junction_box_to_indicator: "750 m/mm²"? Wait that's odd: "750 m/mm₂" — that looks like a length per cross-section spec: 750 m/mm². Actually typical spec is like "(length × cross-section) ≤ ..." Hmm, in R76, the load cell cable constraint is expressed as length in m times cross-section in mm² ≤ some value. Actually the standard formulation: "cable length in meters × cross section in mm² ≥ ..." Something like L·S ≥ 750 m·mm²? Typically the requirement is that the cable resistance doesn't exceed certain values, expressed as e.g. "cable (length × cross-section) ≤ 500 m·mm²"? Hmm. Anyway, keep as raw: value 750, unit "m/mm²". I'll record with unit_symbol "m/mm²".
  Alternative: 1.5 m.

Power supply: "100VAC-230VAC, 50 / 60 Hz" → voltage {min:100, max:230} V, type AC, frequency {min:50, max:60} Hz.

Devices list: could be captured as description or characteristics string list. Maybe include in certified_type.description or a type_level characteristic "devices" with string value? The schema characteristics values must be structured objects. Device list could go in matrix? Simplest: include in description. I'll augment description.

Model family? The cert covers one indicator model WPI-700 with two construction variants. Not >1 model variant per se; WPI-701/702 are instrument designations using it. I'd not create model_family; use config_level for construction axis. Actually rule 5 says config axes for variations like this. Good.
